quizzes.title: 27.1 Module 27 Introduction: The Soviet Collapse
quizzes.description:
MODULE INTRODUCTION
Module Introduction: The Soviet Collapse
Survey · 2 questions · not graded
❅ ─ ❅ ─ ❅
Before you start

Welcome to The Soviet Collapse. Answer the questions below before you open the first lesson. Your answers help your teacher see where the class is starting. This survey is not graded.

This module's goals:
  • Describe detente, the war in Afghanistan, the rise of Solidarity, and Reagan’s policy toward Moscow.
  • Explain the reforms of Gorbachev, the revolutions of 1989, and the end of the Soviet Union.
  • Weigh which pressures on the Soviet system came from outside and which from within.

questions.text: Before you read: Did Reagan win the Cold War, or did the Soviet Union lose it? Give your first answer in two or three sentences. You will answer it again at the end of the module, so it is fine if your answer changes.
I have read this module's goals and I know what I am working toward this week.

answers.text: Yes, I have read them
Not yet, I will read them before the first lesson

quizzes.title: 27.7 Reading Quiz: The Soviet Collapse
quizzes.description:
READING QUIZ
Reading Quiz: The Soviet Collapse
7 questions · 7 points
❅ ─ ❅ ─ ❅
Before you start

This quiz covers both lessons and both primary sources for this module. It has 7 questions. Most ask you to work something out from what you read, not to find a sentence in the text. You may look back at the lessons and sources while you work.

HOW TO WORK
Read the two lessons and the two primary sources first, and keep your notes in My Notebook. Then answer the questions below.

questions.text: The Soviets wanted the Helsinki Final Act of 1975 because it recognized the borders set after the war. Why did it turn out to work against them?

answers.text: It ended the arms race, so the Soviets had no weapons to use against their neighbors
It gave the West the right to station troops in Eastern Europe
It made the Soviet Union a member of NATO
Its pledge to respect human rights gave dissidents in Moscow, Prague, and Warsaw a standard by which to judge their governments

questions.text: In December 1980 the Soviet leaders discussed invading Poland and decided against it. Which reason does the lesson give?

answers.text: Afghanistan was already costing the Soviet Union too much
Solidarity had already agreed to dissolve itself
The United States had promised to defend Poland with troops
Poland’s government had asked the Soviets to stay out

questions.text: John Paul II visited Poland in June 1979, and many Poles said afterward that it changed how they saw themselves. According to the lesson, what did they see?

answers.text: That the Pope could remove the Polish government
That the Church would soon be allowed to run the country
How many of them there were, and that they were not alone
That the Soviet army would leave Poland that year

questions.text: General Jaruzelski declared martial law in December 1981 and banned Solidarity. What does the lesson say this showed?

answers.text: That the Polish people had given up their hopes for a free union
That the government could rule by force but not by consent, and that the union survived underground with the help of the Church
That the Soviet army had occupied Poland
That Solidarity had been defeated for good

questions.text: Reagan said, “Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall!” The wall stood for two more years. Which reading of the speech does the excerpt best support?

answers.text: It was a threat of war, since Reagan promised to destroy the wall by force
It was a plan agreed in advance with Gorbachev
It asked Gorbachev for a clear public act and proved that the wall would fall within weeks
It welcomed some of what Gorbachev had done and asked for one clear public act, so it offered a way forward as well as a demand

questions.text: Gorbachev meant glasnost to help the Communist Party. Why does the lesson say it worked against him?

answers.text: It let the Party control the newspapers more tightly
It showed the Party’s crimes and failures, as at Chernobyl, so that many citizens stopped trusting what they were told
It led the United States to cut off all trade with the Soviet Union
It gave the old Party leaders more power over the republics

questions.text: A student argues that the Soviet empire in Eastern Europe fell because its rulers chose not to use force. Which evidence from “Gorbachev, 1989, and the End of the Soviet Union” best supports this?

answers.text: At Leipzig the police were ready to fire on seventy thousand marchers and did not, and Soviet troops stayed in their barracks, while in Beijing the rulers sent tanks into Tiananmen Square and kept power
Germany was reunified on October 3, 1990, and stayed in NATO
Boris Yeltsin was elected president of the Russian republic in June 1991
The price of oil fell sharply in 1986

Confirm your submissions. Check each item you have finished.

discussions.title: 27.8 Discussion: Did Reagan win, or did the Soviet Union lose?
discussions.html:
DISCUSSION
Did Reagan win, or did the Soviet Union lose?
Outside pressure or inside collapse?
Graded discussion · 10 points · one post and one reply
❅ ─ ❅ ─ ❅
HOW TO WORK
Read the two lessons and the two primary sources first, and look over your notes in My Notebook. Then post your answer to the prompt below, and reply to one classmate.
DISCUSSION PROMPT

This week’s question: Did Reagan win the Cold War, or did the Soviet Union lose it?

Choose one answer. Use your list of pressures. Name one pressure from outside and one from within that bear on your answer, with the dates and the people involved. Then take up the choice at Leipzig and Beijing in 1989. Say what might have followed if the men in Moscow had used force, as the men in Beijing did.

Write 150 to 250 words. State one claim you believe is true. Then explain why, using the specific evidence named above. Keep to what the lessons and the sources show. If you are guessing, say so.

Then add one sentence on courage. Name one person or group in these lessons who stood up when it was dangerous, and say what it risked.

RESPOND TO A CLASSMATE

Reply to one classmate. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with a fact or decision they did not use. If not, say politely where you think it falls short, and give your reason.

GRADING RUBRIC (10 pts)
CriteriaSubstantive (full credit)Thin (partial credit)Missing (no credit)
Your claim and your reasons
6 pts		Takes a clear side, uses the specific evidence the prompt asks for, and explains why it supports the claim.Takes a side but gives general reasons, or leaves out part of what the prompt asks for.No post, or no claim.
Your reply to a classmate
4 pts		Answers one classmate's actual reasoning. Strengthens it or says where it falls short, politely and with a reason.Replies, but only to agree or disagree with no reason.No reply.
10 pts total
